options: To record transactions that already have an invoice or receipt
To cancel out mistakes made earlier in the period
To replace the need for a trial balance
To capture events that happened but have no natural paper trail yet, keeping the books aligned with the matching principle
questions.explain: Adjusting entries capture period-end events — like unbilled accrued wages — that don't have an invoice or receipt of their own, so financial statements stay accurate.

questions.q: Larkspur Retail Group's employees earn $3,000 of wages in the last days of March, but payroll doesn't run until April 5. What is the March 31 adjusting entry?
options: Debit Wages Payable $3,000; Credit Wages Expense $3,000
Debit Wages Expense $3,000; Credit Wages Payable $3,000
Debit Cash $3,000; Credit Wages Expense $3,000
No entry is needed until the cash is actually paid
questions.explain: The wages expense is incurred in March, so it's debited, with a corresponding liability (Wages Payable) credited since it hasn't been paid yet.

questions.q: What would happen to March's financial statements if the wage accrual adjusting entry were skipped?
options: Expenses would be overstated by $3,000
There would be no effect on March's statements
Expenses would be understated and net income overstated by $3,000
Revenue would be understated by $3,000
questions.explain: Without the accrual, March's books would be missing $3,000 of expense that actually belongs there, understating expenses and overstating net income.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a reversing entry, dated the first day of the new period?
options: To flip the adjusting entry so the later real transaction doesn't double-count the same amount
To permanently delete the original adjusting entry
To record a brand-new, unrelated transaction
To correct an unbalanced journal entry
questions.explain: A reversing entry cancels out the adjustment so that when the real transaction is recorded later, the combined effect comes out correct without double-counting.

questions.q: How does Oracle Fusion General Ledger relate to reversing entries?
options: Oracle Fusion has no concept of reversing entries at all
It requires every reversing entry to be manually re-typed from scratch
It only allows reversing entries for revenue, never expenses
It has a built-in feature to automatically reverse a flagged journal entry on a chosen date, automating this exact pattern
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion General Ledger can flag a journal to reverse automatically on a specified date, automating the manual reversing-entry pattern.
